newsitem.title: BURUNDI: Heavy shelling rocks east Zaire town.
newsitem.headline: Heavy shelling rocks east Zaire town.

text.p: Heavy shelling rocked the east Zairean town of Uvira overnight and on Friday from fighting between the Zairean army and ethnic Tutsi rebels, Bujumbura residents said.
The shelling, audible in the Burundian capital 30 km (18 miles) to the east across Lake Tanganyika, began late on Thursday night and continued from 7 a.m. (0500 GMT) on Friday.
"It was almost certainly mortar fire because of the sound of the rockets," said an aid worker, adding it was unclear if the shelling was an attempt by Banyamulenge rebels to take control of Uvira.
More than 200,000 Rwandan and Burundian refugees fled camps north of Uvira towards the city of Bukavu in the past week because of fighting between the Zairean army and Banyamulenge rebels.
The U.N. airlifted the last 58 foreign aid workers out of Uvira on Tuesday as the Banyamulenge rebels pushed northwards.
All equipment owned by U.N. and other aid agencies including vehicles and office equipment was looted within 24 hours of the aid workers leaving, said Chris Anderson of Care International.
